arxiv-1908-03781.title: A theory of incremental compression Journal: Information Sciences
arxiv-1908-03781.creator: Arthur Franz, Oleksandr Antonenko, Roman Soletskyi
arxiv-1908-03781.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Arthur Franz, Oleksandr Antonenko, Roman Soletskyi. The ability to find short representations, i.e. to compress data, is crucial for many intelligent systems. We present a theory of incremental compression showing that arbitrary data strings, that can be described by a set of features, can be compressed by searching for those features incrementally, which results in a partition of the information content of the string into a complete set of pairwise independent pieces.

arxiv-2109-09237.title: MirrorWiC : On Eliciting Word-in-Context Representations from Pretrained Language Models
arxiv-2109-09237.creator: Qianchu Liu, Fangyu Liu, Nigel Collier, Anna Korhonen, Ivan VulićLanguage Technology Lab, TAL, University of Cambridge {ql261, fl399, nhc30, alk23, iv250}@cam.ac.uk
arxiv-2109-09237.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Qianchu Liu, Fangyu Liu, Nigel Collier, Anna Korhonen, Ivan VulićLanguage Technology Lab, TAL, University of Cambridge {ql261, fl399, nhc30, alk23, iv250}@cam.ac.uk. Recent work indicated that pretrained language models (PLMs) such as BERT and RoBERTa can be transformed into effective sentence and word encoders even via simple self-supervised techniques. Inspired by this line of work, in this paper we propose a fully unsupervised approach to improving word-in-context (WiC) representations in PLMs, achieved via a simple and efficient WiC-targeted fine-tuning procedure: MirrorWiC .

arxiv-2310-20632.title: Constrained Planarity in Practice DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2310-20632.creator: Simon D. Fink, Ignaz Rutter
arxiv-2310-20632.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Simon D. Fink, Ignaz Rutter. In the constrained planarity setting, we ask whether a graph admits a planar drawing that additionally satisfies a given set of constraints. These constraints are often derived from very natural problems; prominent examples are Level Planarity , where vertices have to lie on given horizontal lines indicating a hierarchy, and Clustered Planarity , where we additionally draw the boundaries of clusters which recursively group the vertices in a crossing-free manner.

arxiv-2509-20816.title: Accelerating the Monte Carlo simulation of the Enskog equation for multiscale dense gas flows
arxiv-2509-20816.creator: Bin Hu, Liyan Luo, Lei Wu
arxiv-2509-20816.description: Abstract A general synthetic iterative scheme is proposed to solve the Enskog equation within a Monte Carlo framework. The method demonstrates rapid convergence by reducing intermediate Monte Carlo evolution and preserves the asymptotic-preserving property, enabling spatial cell sizes much larger than the mean free path in near-continuum flows.
